name: Rite of Strength
summary: At Camp Narache, young tauren face the Rite of Strength against Bristleback quilboar. They bring their belts to Chief Hawkwind to prove their courage and defend the tribe.

sections.title: The First Trial
sections.body: Seer Graytongue calls young tauren to begin the Rites of the Earthmother with the Rite of Strength. Those who seek recognition from the tribal elders and acceptance in Thunder Bluff must face this duty. The trial tests whether an initiate can meet the tribe's mortal foes with courage and act to defend Red Cloud Mesa.

sections.title: The Bristleback Threat
sections.body: East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is home to Bristleback quilboar. The quilboar trespass on ancestral lands, ambush hunting parties, and raid camp supplies under cover of darkness. You are asked to slay them and bring back their belts. The proof shows your valor and helps keep the settlement secure.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Rite of Strength?
faq.answer: The Rite of Strength tests a young tauren's courage in combat as the first step in the Rites of the Earthmother. Defeating threats to the camp earns an initiate the right to continue toward respect in Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Who assigns and judges this trial?
aliases: who turns in rite of strength
faq.answer: Seer Graytongue gives the charge and explains its spiritual and practical demands. Bring twelve Bristleback belts to Chief Hawkwind at Camp Narache as proof of valor.
Brambleblade Ravine lies east of Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Its thorny canyon is home to hostile Bristleback quilboar.

faq.q: Why are the Bristlebacks being targeted?
faq.answer: The Bristlebacks trespass on the tribe's ancestral hunting grounds. They ambush tauren hunters and steal provisions from Camp Narache in the dark, making them enemies of the tribe.

faq.q: Why collect belts instead of other trophies?
faq.answer: The belts are proof that an initiate faced the quilboar and defeated their adult warriors in close combat, rather than scavenging from a distance.

faq.q: What comes after completing the Rite of Strength?
aliases: what is after rite of strength
faq.answer: Passing the Rite of Strength proves an initiate's valor and qualifies them for the next trials of the Earthmother. These trials continue the formal path to adulthood and spiritual standing within the tribe.

angles.text: As a young tauren, you begin the ancient rites by showing you can defend your people from the quilboar before leaving Red Cloud Mesa.
As a member of the Horde, you help defend Red Cloud Mesa, one of its core recruiting grounds, so young warriors and shamans can mature safely and aid the new union.
